title: 3D Vision, NeRFs & Gaussian Splatting
tagline: Turn photos into 3D: camera geometry, stereo, structure from motion, depth networks, neural radiance fields, Gaussian splatting, and feed-forward reconstruction.
prereqs: Computer Vision. Python & Math for AI (linear algebra). Deep Learning for the NeRF and splatting code. Training steps want an NVIDIA GPU or a cloud GPU.

steps.title: Pinhole cameras and perspective projection
steps.why: How a 3D point lands on a 2D image, the base of everything after.

steps.title: Camera intrinsics and extrinsics
steps.why: The two matrices that describe a camera's lens and its pose.

steps.title: Depth from stereo
steps.why: Two calibrated cameras plus disparity give you depth by triangulation.

steps.title: Epipolar geometry
steps.why: The constraint linking matching points across two uncalibrated views.

steps.title: Structure from motion with COLMAP
steps.why: Recover camera poses and sparse 3D points from a photo collection.

steps.title: Depth from a single image
steps.why: How neural networks learn to guess depth from one photo.

steps.title: Deep learning on 3D data
steps.why: Stanford CS231n lecture on voxels, point clouds, meshes, and implicit shapes.

steps.title: Neural radiance fields (NeRF)
steps.why: A network that maps position and view direction to color and density.

steps.title: Code NeRF in 100 lines of PyTorch
steps.why: Ray sampling, volume rendering, and training, written out in short code.

steps.title: Train a NeRF on your own scene
steps.why: Capture, train, and export a mesh with the open-source Nerfstudio toolkit.

steps.title: 3D Gaussian splatting
steps.why: Swap the network for millions of 3D Gaussians that rasterize in real time.

steps.title: Code Gaussian splatting in PyTorch
steps.why: Projection, sorting, and alpha blending of Gaussians in about 300 lines.

steps.title: From your video to a splat with free tools
steps.why: A practical capture-to-viewer pipeline using RealityScan, Brush, and SuperSplat.

steps.title: Feed-forward reconstruction: DUSt3R and MASt3R
steps.why: Talk by a co-author: one network predicts 3D points from image pairs.

steps.title: Generating 3D models with diffusion
steps.why: How 2D diffusion models are used to create new 3D objects.

projects: Calibrate your phone camera with a printed checkerboard in OpenCV and report its focal length and distortion.
Photograph one object from 40 angles, reconstruct it with COLMAP, then train both a NeRF and a Gaussian splat and compare quality and render speed.
Run Depth Anything V2 on 20 of your photos and turn three of them into point clouds you can rotate in a viewer.
